title: Electronic Properties of Parallelly Aligned Arrays of Carbon Nanotubes
content: We present results of DFT calculations of electronic properties, i.e. band structure, density of states and energy gap for arrays of parallelly ordered infinitely long small-diameter carbon nanotubes (CNTs). It turns out that if the distance between CNTs is sufficiently large (of the order 7.5\AA or greater), the electronic properties of arrays  are very close to isolated CNTs. However, when in arrays CNTs are forced to be at a distance of the order of 5 \AA, they undergo radical structural rearrangement, leading to completely different structures: graphene-like or intermediate between graphite and diamond. Electronic properties are also rebuilt in a drastic manner.
